findings: Prop 9.1 (l.2575–2577) says 'stabilizes an isotropic vector', its proof (l.2593–2594) 'stabilizes a lightlike direction', §9.2 (l.2621) 'preserves an isotropic vector v₀': the readings agree only because an element of SO₀ scaling a null vector by λ ≠ 1 is loxodromic, which the paper never states.

labels.label: bprop:U_timelike
findings: Prop 10.4's proof (l.3356–3359): 'an abelian subgroup of SO₀(1,n−1) fixes a pair of isotropic directions, except if it consists only of elliptic elements' is false for n ≥ 3: the cyclic group of a null rotation is abelian, not elliptic, and fixes exactly one point of 𝒮 (not_abelianPairAsPrinted, DEC-27). The proof survives: one invariant isotropic direction already contradicts the [10.G] hypothesis (l.3336–3337) — but the corrected folklore needs, for parabolic R∘U with R ≠ id and for all-elliptic abelian groups, the trichotomy (not formalized here).

kb_proposals: An external is a Prop with two witnesses: 'not false' (here at d = 0, where SO₀(1,0) is trivial and 𝒮 is empty — degenerate, it shows consistency only: lorentz_zero_eq_one, isEmpty_penroseSphere_zero) and 'not trivially true' (its conclusion fails once a hypothesis is dropped — the cyclic group of a boost, discreteTopology_zpowers_stdBoostL; Isom(Mⁿ) itself for the nilpotency hypothesis; the infinite torsion group of root-of-unity rotations of ℂ for finite generation).
